main_text.p: Quomodo Christum deformarunt illæ manus? imò Crucem: & sic mihi libido aliquando legere: sed refræno, & accipio Christum crucifixum. Hæc illa est quam Crux AndreanaAndreanam hodie dicimus, validâ & satis veteri famâ divum istum in eâ cruciatum. Anne verâ? facit me ut ambigam Martyrologium Romanum: in quo *vt & hoc saltem *legas,in Cruce suspensum. & magis Hippolytus in Abdia lib. iii., qui scribit Crucifixum Patris in Achaiâ, ad arborem oliuæ rectum. Quid magis contra famam? Atque hæc fixio ad Simplicem nostram potiùs abeat, longè à Decussatâ.

page.notes: Marginal marks and catchwords in the left margin are partly faint; "Crux Andreana" and "Andreana" read from the small-type marginal heads. The Greek footnote reference is printed as "¹" and the note text "In Comment. Græco." is transcribed as printed. Some letters are smudged, notably in "Hippolytus" and "Achaiâ". Numerals "iii." and the Abdia reference are uncertain.
